name: library
description: The books. They live in the `books` table (readTier cold, never boot-loaded) and are read two ways over one shelf: the tablet's LIBRARY app (plugins/tablet/library-app.js) and this plugin's typed reader (`library`/`read`/`page`/`chapter`/`contents`). Both call plugins/library/books.js and share the `book_pos_<id>` bookmark, so a book put down in one is picked up in the other. SCAN at furniture tagged `lending_terminal` sets the `library_unlocked` player flag, which gates BOTH front ends — before that the app is not on the home screen and the verbs fall through. The first scan prints an intro covering narration, minimize-and-keep-reading, the tap-to-gloss vocabulary layer, and per-book bookmarks; later scans are a gentle no-op. Examining a terminal teaches the verb once via the house shimmer convention. Leaf plugin: no table, no tick.

read.note: Shared verb — self-gates on a shelf title AND on `library_unlocked`, returning undefined so the bulletin/jail/jobboard/cooking readers still get their turn. Bare `read` deliberately falls through.

longbox.note: The comics, on a listing of their own (`books.kind='comic'`). A presentation split only — `read <title>` matches across BOTH shelves, so nothing is harder to reach for having been separated.

page.note: Pagination is the typed reader's alone (`book_page_<id>`); the tablet scrolls a whole chapter and has no concept of a page, so teaching it one would make the two readers disagree about where you are.
